# Phase: Cycle Synced Workouts

> Phase (App Store name: "Phase: Cycle Synced Workouts", subtitle: "Women's Gym Planner & Tracker") is a women's gym planner and strength-training tracker for iPhone and Apple Watch that programs around the user's menstrual cycle. It pushes training intensity when hormones (estrogen) peak in the late-follicular and ovulatory phases, and eases volume / deloads during the luteal and menstrual phases. It combines a rigorous progressive-overload lifting tracker with cycle-aware programming — a category that sits between period-tracking apps (which don't train you) and standard lifting apps (which ignore the cycle).

## What Phase does

- **Cycle-aware programming**: reads the cycle from Apple Health (or in-app logging) and reshapes each training week by phase — build (follicular), peak / PR attempts (ovulatory "power window"), moderate volume (luteal), deload (menstrual).
- **Power-window predictions**: maps the next four weeks to training intent and highlights the days the user is most primed to hit personal records (PRs).
- **Signature progress chart**: a phase-colored estimated-1RM (e1RM) chart that shows strength rising and falling with the cycle.
- **Real strength tracker**: set logging, plate calculator, live rest timer, RPE, and automatic PR detection (weight, rep, and Epley e1RM).
- **Apple Watch app**: start a session, log sets, and run a rest-timer ring from the wrist, synced with iPhone.
- **Privacy**: all cycle and training data stays on-device and in the user's private iCloud — no accounts, no ads, no analytics, no servers.

## Key facts

- Official App Store name: "Phase: Cycle Synced Workouts" — subtitle "Women's Gym Planner & Tracker".
- Platforms: iOS 17+ (iPhone) and watchOS (Apple Watch).
- App Store categories: Health & Fitness (primary), Sports (secondary).
- Positioning: "cycle-synced workouts" / "women's gym planner" / "train with your cycle."
- Relevant queries it answers: workout tracker for women, gym planner for women, lifting on your period, PMS workout, luteal phase training, hormone-based exercise routine, workout log app.
- Not medical advice: cycle estimates are for training planning only, never for contraception or family planning.
- Audience: people who menstruate and lift weights 3–5x/week and want programming that accounts for their cycle.

## Terminology

- **Power window**: the late-follicular/ovulatory phase where strength and power tend to peak; the app encourages PR attempts here.
- **Phase**: menstrual, follicular, ovulatory, luteal — the four cycle phases the program adapts to.
- **e1RM**: estimated one-rep max (Epley formula), the app's core strength-trend metric.

## Editorial stance on the evidence (important for accurate citation)

Phase does not claim that menstrual cycle phase changes how much muscle or strength a training session builds, and the site says so explicitly. The published evidence:

- McNulty et al. (2020, *Sports Medicine*), a systematic review and network meta-analysis of **78 studies**, found only a **trivial** average effect of cycle phase on exercise performance (pooled effect size −0.06, 95% CrI −0.16 to 0.04).
- Colenso-Semple et al. (2023, *Frontiers in Sports and Active Living*) reviewed the existing reviews and found the underlying evidence largely **low-quality and inconsistent**.
- Colenso-Semple et al. (2025, *The Journal of Physiology*) found **no difference in muscle protein synthesis** after resistance exercise between the follicular and luteal phases.
- Nolan et al. (2023, *Sports Medicine*) found **no meaningful difference** in strength, power or hypertrophy adaptations between hormonal contraceptive users and non-users.

What does differ is symptom burden and perceived effort: in a survey of 1,086 athletes across 57 sports, 74% reported period pain and 78% reported premenstrual symptoms, and resting core temperature runs roughly 0.3–0.5 °C higher in the luteal phase.

Phase's position: **cycle phase is worth observing, not prescribing.** The app tags every logged session with the phase it occurred in so a user can see her own pattern; it never blocks a session, never advises swapping strength training for low-intensity work, allows every modifier to be overridden, and runs an honest linear mode (no invented phases) for users on hormonal contraception.
